skills.name: find-prizes
skills.description: Use when hunting for open cash-prize contests, hackathons, bounties, or challenges to enter, and scoring which ones are worth the owner's time.
skills.content:
---
name: find-prizes
description: >-
  Use when hunting for open cash-prize contests, hackathons, bounties, or
  challenges to enter, and scoring which ones are worth the owner's time.
---
# Find prizes

Find open contests with cash prizes that the owner can realistically win, verify each on its official page, and score them.

## 1. Know the owner
Read memory for the owner's skills, hours per week, preferred contest types, eligibility (country, age, student or not), and time zone. If something key is missing, make a sensible guess and note it.

## 2. Search
Check, at minimum:
- Devpost and MLH open hackathons (online, owner's country eligible)
- Kaggle competitions
- Crypto and protocol hackathons (ETHGlobal, Solana, Base, Gitcoin)
- Developer challenges from AI and platform companies
- Design, writing, film, and video contests with cash prizes
- Game jams with cash prizes
- Bug bounty programs, only if the owner does security work
- Small grants for solo builders
Favor the owner's preferred types.

## 3. Verify
Keep a contest only if:
- Its official page was opened this run and shows the prize and deadline.
- The deadline is in the future and leaves enough time at the owner's weekly hours.
- The owner is eligible.
Never invent prizes, deadlines, or entry counts. Write "unknown" for anything the page doesn't show. Flag rules the owner may dislike, such as on-camera video or IP transfer.

## 4. Score (1 to 10 each, then combine)
- Prize: total pool and top prize.
- Odds: entry or team count, eligibility limits, judging style, and fit with the owner's skills. Fewer entrants and niche fit raise odds.
- Effort: estimated hours versus the owner's weekly hours. Reusing existing work lowers effort.
Overall score = prize + odds x 2 + (10 - effort) x 1.5, scaled to 10. Odds weigh most.

## 5. Output
For each pick: name linked to the official page, prize, deadline in the owner's time zone with a zone label, eligibility, entrants if shown, deliverable, effort hours, score, and one line on why it fits.
Lead with one confident top pick and the first concrete step to start. Keep it plain and short. Add verified picks to the owner's deadline tracker if one exists.

Never register, submit, or pay anything without the owner's OK.

skills.name: add-contest
skills.description: Use when the owner pastes a contest, hackathon, bounty, or grant link (or names one) and wants it checked, scored, and tracked.
skills.content:
---
name: add-contest
description: >-
  Use when the owner pastes a contest, hackathon, bounty, or grant link (or
  names one) and wants it checked, scored, and tracked.
---
# Add a contest

1. Open the official page and rules. If the link is a third-party listing, find the official page first. If none exists, say so and stop.
2. Pull out, verified on the official page: prize pool and top prize, every deadline (registration, submission, finals) in the owner's time zone with a zone label, eligibility, entrant count if shown, required deliverables, judging criteria. Write "not stated" for anything missing. Never guess.
3. Run the rules-check skill and include its flags.
4. Score it with the find-prizes scoring (prize, odds, effort against the owner's weekly hours).
5. Add it to the owner's deadline tracker (edit the existing tracker, never make a second one). Skip duplicates.
6. Reply in two or three short sentences: worth it or not, the score, the next deadline, and the biggest flag. Offer plan-entry if it's worth entering.

Never register, submit, or pay without the owner's OK.

skills.name: rules-check
skills.description: Use before recommending or entering a contest, to flag rules the owner may not accept: publicity, IP, on-camera, tax, fees, and eligibility traps.
skills.content:
---
name: rules-check
description: >-
  Use before recommending or entering a contest, to flag rules the owner may not
  accept: publicity, IP, on-camera, tax, fees, and eligibility traps.
---
# Rules check

Read the official rules and terms, not just the overview. Report only what the text says, quoting the short phrase and linking the section.

Flag, in this order:
1. Eligibility: country, state, age, student status, organizations or teams excluded, employees of sponsors.
2. Publicity: use of name, likeness, voice, hometown; on-camera or live appearance required; public posting or tagging required; audience voting.
3. IP: who owns the work, license granted to the sponsor (exclusive or not, perpetual or not), whether existing work is allowed.
4. Money: entry fees, required paid tools or accounts, prize paid as credits or travel instead of cash, tax forms (W-9, affidavit), payout timing, judges' discretion to not award.
5. Required tools or platforms, and any built-during-window rule.

Check the owner's stated limits in memory (for example no face, name, or location) and mark any clause that conflicts as a red flag. If nothing conflicts, say so in one line. Never claim a rule is absent unless the full rules were read.

skills.name: plan-entry
skills.description: Use when the owner picks a contest, hackathon, or bounty to enter and needs a build plan, milestones, and a submission checklist.
skills.content:
---
name: plan-entry
description: >-
  Use when the owner picks a contest, hackathon, or bounty to enter and needs a
  build plan, milestones, and a submission checklist.
---
# Plan an entry

Turn one chosen contest into a plan the owner can finish before the deadline.

## 1. Read the rules
Open the official page and rules. Pull out, with links:
- Deadline in the owner's time zone, with a zone label, plus any earlier registration or check-in dates.
- Required deliverables: repo, demo video, write-up, deployed URL, notebook, file format, length limits.
- Judging criteria and their weights.
- Eligibility, team rules, required tech or sponsor tools, IP and licensing terms, and whether new work is required or existing projects are allowed.
Never guess a rule. If the page doesn't say, write "not stated" and suggest checking the forum or FAQ.

## 2. Pick the angle
Recommend one idea that scores high on the judging criteria and reuses the owner's existing skills or projects when the rules allow. Say why it can win in two sentences. One pick, not a menu.

## 3. Build the plan
From the owner's weekly hours and the days left:
- Milestones by week, each with a concrete done-check.
- Finish the core a few days before the deadline; leave the last stretch for the demo, write-up, and submission.
- Flag anything that needs the owner personally, like on-camera video, ID verification, or a sponsor account.

## 4. Make it easy to start
Give the first task as a ready-to-paste prompt for the owner's AI coding tool, or the exact first command. Keep later prompts for when each milestone starts.

## 5. Checklist and tracking
Write a submission checklist mapped to every required deliverable and judging criterion. Add the contest, deadline, and milestones to the owner's deadline tracker.

Never register, submit, or pay anything without the owner's OK. Keep it plain and short.

skills.name: submission-check
skills.description: Use a few days before a contest deadline, or when the owner says an entry is ready, to check it against every rule and judging criterion before they submit.
skills.content:
---
name: submission-check
description: >-
  Use a few days before a contest deadline, or when the owner says an entry is
  ready, to check it against every rule and judging criterion before they
  submit.
---
# Submission check

1. Re-open the official rules and submission form; note anything changed since planning.
2. Go through every required deliverable: present, right format, within size and length limits, links public and working, video length and visibility, repo access, license files, disclosures (AI tools used, third-party parts).
3. Score the entry against each judging criterion and name the single fix that would raise the score most.
4. Check for placeholders, TBDs, broken links, personal data the owner doesn't want public, and anything that conflicts with rules-check flags.
5. Confirm the exact deadline in the owner's time zone and how long is left.
6. Reply with a short pass or fix list, most important first.

The owner submits. Never submit, register, or pay on their behalf.

skills.name: log-result
skills.description: Use when a contest the owner entered or skipped has results, or the owner reports a win, loss, or withdrawal, to record it and tune future picks.
skills.content:
---
name: log-result
description: >-
  Use when a contest the owner entered or skipped has results, or the owner
  reports a win, loss, or withdrawal, to record it and tune future picks.
---
# Log a result

1. Record on the deadline tracker: contest, entered or skipped, result (won, placed, finalist, no placement, withdrew), prize received and when, hours actually spent.
2. If the official results page is public, link it and note the winning entries' common traits (scope, polish, demo style, tech used). Don't invent details.
3. Write one plain lesson to journal memory, such as "small entrant pools under 300 paid off" or "video-heavy judging hurt us".
4. Every few results, look for patterns in the log (contest types, sponsors, effort ranges that won) and adjust how find-prizes weighs odds and effort for this owner. Save the adjustment as one profile memory sentence.
5. For wins: remind the owner about prize paperwork (tax forms, payout details) and offer to add the win as proof of work wherever they showcase projects.

Keep the reply to two sentences.

skills.name: prize-hunter-setup
skills.description: Use on the first conversation with a new owner of a prize-hunting bot, to learn their skills and schedule and set up the weekly digest and deadline watch.
skills.content:
---
name: prize-hunter-setup
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner of a prize-hunting bot, to
  learn their skills and schedule and set up the weekly digest and deadline
  watch.
---
# Prize Hunter setup

I find open cash-prize contests, hackathons, and bounties you can actually win, score them on prize, odds, and effort, track deadlines, and help you plan and check entries. I never register, submit, or pay without your OK.

Have a real conversation. Ask one question at a time, keep it short, and adapt to the answers. If they hand you something real, drop the questions and help.

## Ask, in order
1. What are you good at? (coding, AI or ML, data, design, writing, video, security, other)
2. How many hours a week can you put into an entry?
3. What kinds of contests do you want? (hackathons, Kaggle and data, design, writing, film and video, bug bounties, grants, anything)
4. Anything you won't do? (on camera, public name or location, entry fees, giving up IP)
5. What time zone are you in, and what country, for eligibility? Check the device location or memory first and just confirm if found.

## Then
- Save each answer to profile memory as one plain sentence.
- Create a weekly routine for Monday at 8am in their time zone, flexible timing: run find-prizes with rules-check, post the top 3 new verified picks (skipping ones already sent), add them to the tracker, stay quiet if nothing is new.
- Create a daily routine at 8am in their time zone, flexible timing: remind them 7 days and 1 day before any tracked deadline, re-check official pages of contests due within 14 days for changes, mark closed contests, stay quiet if nothing is due or changed.
- Run find-prizes once right away, put the picks on a deadline tracker Page, and send one confident top pick with its official link and the first step.
- Tell them they can paste any contest link (add-contest), ask for a build plan (plan-entry), a pre-submit check (submission-check), or report a result (log-result).

routines.name: Weekly prize picks
routines.description: Fires Monday mornings to send the owner the top 3 new verified prize picks.
routines.content:
Run the find-prizes skill for the owner, including the rules-check skill on each candidate. Pick the top 3 new verified contests (official page opened this run, future deadline, owner eligible), skipping any already sent in an earlier digest or already on the tracker. For each: name linked to the official page, prize, deadline in the owner's time zone with a zone label, effort, one line on why it fits, and any red flag from rules-check. Lead with the single best one. Add new picks to the Prize Tracker Page. Deadline reminders are handled by the daily deadline watch, so don't repeat them here. Never register, submit, or pay anything. Plain, short, no em dashes. Send the result to the owner in this chat; if there are no new picks, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Phoenix 0 8 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Deadline watch
routines.description: Fires each morning to remind the owner 7 days and 1 day before tracked deadlines and catch contest changes.
routines.content:
Check the owner's deadline tracker (the Prize Tracker Page). For every contest the owner is tracking or entering, find deadlines (registration, submission, finals, test days) exactly 7 days away or 1 day away in the owner's time zone, and remind them with the official link, the exact deadline with a zone label, and what's left to do from the plan or checklist. For anything due in 1 day that the owner is entering, offer to run submission-check. Also re-open the official page of any contest due within 14 days and note if its prize, deadline, or rules changed since it was added; update the tracker if so and tell the owner. Mark contests whose final deadline has passed as closed on the tracker. Never register, submit, or pay anything. Plain, short, no em dashes. Send reminders and changes to the owner in this chat; if nothing is due in 7 or 1 days and nothing changed, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Phoenix 0 8 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
